title: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

sense.text:
Every day two things are happening inside a repenting Israelite at the same time. From the day you are born you are on a path to death: you peak, and then everything starts to break down. The outward man perishes day by day, the flesh never stands still, the cares of this world are always pressing, temptations always rise, and sin is always deceptive. Left alone, the natural man does not drift towards God; he drifts away from him. At the same time the spirit has to be renewed daily. Many think they repented once and that is it, but everything pressing on you means you have to counteract it every day.

We understand this with the body. You eat every day, because when you don't, you weaken. A person who diets and trains for months to reach a goal has to keep eating right and training to keep it, or they yo-yo back. Yet many come to the Sabbath, treat it like church, get their classes, and then go a whole week starving the spirit. You would never eat once a week and think that one meal will carry you to the next. Spiritual understanding that is not fed fades, until all that is left is the memory of a precept you memorized. That is how some who quote well and speak great still fade from their walk.

God always designed it this way, from the beginning: “All the commandments which I command thee this day shall ye observe to do, that ye may live, and multiply, and go in and possess the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers.” He requires continual feeding upon his word.

“And thou shalt remember all the way which the Lord thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness.” What happened in the wilderness was to be remembered and taught to every generation, because what happened physically to our forefathers was set there as a witness and an example for us. It was not just history; it happened in such a way, with so many details, that we can learn from their mistakes and apply it today.

“To humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no.” The wilderness was to humble us, to prove us, and to show what is in our heart, much like what we must go through every day in this walk.

“And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only.” We read past this. He fed us manna so that we would know man does not live by bread alone, but wasn't manna a form of bread? So what is he talking about? There is a spiritual element here. The manna represented something that was to nourish us later. It was not about putting literal bread in your mouth every day; it was to teach us that our nourishment depends on God.

“But by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord doth man live.” Every word gave the instructions for surviving the wilderness. That is why the whole adult generation had to die: they did not heed those words, and there was always rebellion. Every word was to show our dependency on God, and that is why it says he humbled us. Where was our dependency before that? Egypt. That is why we kept complaining, in Egypt we had this, in Egypt we had that. This is not our rest.

What was set up with the manna is what we later understand was a foreshadowing of Christ. Christ comes in the volume of the book. Christ is everything, the whole thing, even in the little details of the examples, not only the sacrifices. All of it is symbolic of something related to Christ.

precepts.why:
When Satan tempted Christ in the wilderness, Christ quoted Deuteronomy 8:3: “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.” Written where? In Deuteronomy 8:3.

Christ was weakened and hungry from his fast, and there was a lot going on in that temptation. It was not just to eat; it was to get him to not have God as his supply. Satan would have been the thing that gave him ease in that moment, and Christ knew that was not it. He set the example for us that we lean on the Most High in all these things.

What he is really telling you is what is read much later: the flesh profits nothing; the words are what is real life. That is not an excuse to go starve yourself. But all the prophets understood the parallel: they always spoke of consuming the word, eating the word, how it tasted, how it was in their belly and strengthened them. God wants us to acknowledge our dependence on him, and not just in general, but daily.

sense.text: “And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness”, saying, “Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full.” That is the example: they wanted to go back to Egypt, back to depending on Egypt, not realizing how much greater a thing God had in store for his people.

“Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day.” There was a portion for the day, and it was different for everyone, based on appetite, family size and need, because everybody needs a different level of nourishment. The calories one man eats are not the calories another eats. So it is with the word: like the double portion of oil at the anointing, some of us need more of the word of God than others.

“That I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.” Weren't they keeping the Sabbath days? They were keeping the law, though there were times they broke it and were corrected. What he is really proving is whether they would stay on him daily and seek him as their source and their supply.

“At even ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread; and ye shall know that I am the Lord your God.” He gave them quails in the evening and manna in the morning. Yes, you have to nourish your body, but at the same time you also have to nourish your spirit.

A “small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground”, and “they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was.” The word manna literally means: what is it? That is the literal sense; spiritually it means so much more.

“This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.” What they did not know yet at that moment, and what we need to understand, is that he was talking about Christ. The bread we were given to eat, the spiritual food from heaven, was Christ.

“Gather of it every man according to his eating.” Of all the wondrous things written in the Bible, why does it speak so extensively, with so much attention, about eating? Because there is something more in it for us to pull out and apply in these last days.

“And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some more, some less”, according to their need: some needed more nourishment, some less, some had larger families, some smaller. “He that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating”: according to what each needed for nourishment and appetite.
“Let no man leave of it till the morning.” You were not supposed to store it.

“Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.” Physically, it went bad. If the bread represents the word of God, it is telling you that yesterday's study, yesterday's class, yesterday's nourishment for your spirit is not good for the following day. Not that it has no value; it is not enough. You need to eat every day and be in the word every day, and if you are not, find ways to get in it.

The perfect scenario is four chapters a day, a class, all of it set up, but life does not always come at us that way. You can listen to something. At a bare minimum you can read a couple of verses, and not random ones, not just opening to Psalms and Proverbs and picking something. Whatever is most heavy upon you, seek it out in the scripture and meditate on it. Maybe what you lack is to focus on one or two verses that will get you right in what you are dealing with.

The Bible speaks extensively about bitterness and grudging, yet we still fall into it. That is how you know that somebody who says they are leaving because somebody offended them, but they are going to keep God's laws, is full of crap. They left because they held a grudge and grew bitter. So be careful when feelings come up about people that are personal and not about the sin they are doing. The most seductive and subtle things are not lust; they are emotions, what you feel about others, and the weariness in the mission and in the day-to-day of applying these laws.

Just as the manna went bad every day, the word you read yesterday will not keep you nourished for the next day. When you are not in it, it does not show as hunger or thirst; your mind starts to stray, and your spirit starts to look at things differently. You cannot feed your spirit once a week, or half a week, or every other day. It has to be daily. Then the things most heavy upon you become lighter, and that is how you put off mortal thoughts.

That is what Christ was saying in Matthew 4:4: your spirit needs daily nourishment to survive the wilderness. And make no mistake, this is a wilderness. We are pilgrims and strangers here; this is not our rest. It is a proving ground where we have grace, as our forefathers had forty years of grace to get it together. It is grace to get it right, not grace to do whatever the hell you want.

precepts.why:
“Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.” Usually this is used about children, or about responsibilities in the body. But look at it individually: the idleness is not feeding yourself with the scriptures every day, not doing something spiritual every day.

The flesh is pulling all the time, and when you are idle in the word, evil starts to creep in. You cannot know these things and not nourish your spirit every day, knowing that your flesh is fighting every minute to revive the old man. That is the pattern of people who have been here for years: it does not matter how long you have been here, but what your reputation has been among us, and how easily that can be distorted and lost.

sense.text:
“Give us this day our daily bread.” This is the Lord's prayer, and has anybody ever stopped and asked why, in all of this, he is asking for food? Does anything else in the Lord's prayer pertain to food, or does the prayer pertain to the kingdom of heaven? Deliver us from evil, forgive us our debts, thine is the kingdom and the power: it would seem so out of course in the whole prayer to stop and ask for your food every day.

It is not talking about the food you eat. It is talking about the spiritual, God's word. It is a reminder, in one of the foundation prayers we should have, of the spiritual nourishment we need daily, and it is connected to the history read in Deuteronomy 8 and Exodus 16. It is all a reminder.

“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea.” Everybody says Corinthians was written to Gentiles. Reading is fundamental: if these were Gentiles, how were all their fathers under the cloud in the wilderness? Sometimes it is as simple as that; tell them to explain it. They always find a way, like the pigeon that craps on the board and says it won: now those are their fathers because they are repenting.

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea.” Baptism is the receiving of the laws and then doing the laws, in the faith of Christ. Don't leave Christ out of it: the whole Bible is about Christ, and any time you preach the word of God it is about Christ.
“And did all eat the same spiritual meat”: the manna. They all ate the same spiritual meat, and it is also the spiritual meat of the commandments given to Moses in the cloud.

“And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” The manna represents Christ. Everything that happened to them in the wilderness was the foreshadowing, the setup, to show the dependency we would need on Christ.

“But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” Was there an enemy that overthrew them in the wilderness? No. They were overthrown by their own lust, by the desires of the carnal man that they did not subdue, and by not humbling themselves in the wilderness.

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” How do you avoid lusting after those things? By feeding yourself with the word of God.

Israel needed manna every day to survive the wilderness, and the manna is not telling you to go eat bread every day; it is the word of God. Christ made that comparison in Matthew 4:4. The point is not simply to read your Bible; it is that spiritual life needs consistent, continual nourishment, just as physical life needs continual food. There is no way you would eat on Saturday and not eat again until next Saturday.

So those who think they are ten toes down, who think they will survive when Jacob's trouble magnifies itself on that kind of diet, need to be training all the time for that day. Be the warrior in the garden instead of a gardener in a war. Right now it is trials, and there is a big difference between trials and tribulation; we have not yet striven unto death. See who sticks around when that time comes.

precepts.why:
When they try to tell you about being baptized: “He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.” That is Moses receiving the commandments in the cloud.

Being baptized unto Moses in the cloud was not dipping six hundred thousand men and all the rest into rivers and waters. If anything, where was the water? The Lord had to provide water from a rock. The baptism goes back to the commandments, the law of life and knowledge, and that represents Christ.

sense.text:
The forefathers understood that this was food. You have to want this word like a fat kid loves cake.

“Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips”: I have not gone back; I stay at this word. “I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.” More than the food he had to eat so that he would not die and wither away. God's word is above that.

precepts.why:
“Thy words were found, and I did eat them.” The prophets always spoke of the word this way. You would think it is random, but it all ties back to their foundational understanding of what is read in Deuteronomy and Exodus.

“And thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart: for I am called by thy name, O Lord God of hosts.” Jeremiah understood this.

sense.text: “Son of man, eat that thou findest; eat this roll, and go speak unto the house of Israel.” The messenger, the angel, tells him to eat the roll and then go. The roll is the scroll, the scriptures. Eat this, strengthen yourself, then go speak. The rest of Ezekiel shows the parallel: his forehead was made strong against theirs, because they were stiff-necked and rebellious. Remember, Moses wanted to die dealing with Israel. You have to build yourself up in the spirit, train and be ready, to be able to deal with our people.

“Son of man, cause thy belly to eat, and fill thy bowels with this roll that I give thee.” Fill it. In America the restaurants give portions two or three people could eat off of; at Olive Garden, Applebee's or Chili's, just because they give you that portion of fries does not mean you need to eat them all. With food be mindful, just as the manna was gathered according to need. But that is not the case with God's word. You can stuff yourself with God's word: fill thy bowels.

“Then did I eat it; and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness.” When the manna is described later, it tasted like honey. That is a subtle callback: the word is sweet in our mouth. A lot of times we don't look at that, and we don't meditate on it.

Meditation is not something done once in a while, or only when you are dealing with something. Some things you do are repetitive, and in the moment you won't see the need for them; then when the trial or pressure comes, how you trained and built your spirit shows whether you win that day. Things don't happen to you in this walk; they happen for you, to try you and prove you.

To meditate is to think upon it, muse upon it, keep it with you; not read it and check it off. Take all the meat off the bone. Let the butter melt into every nook of the biscuit instead of biting into a mouthful of butter.

“Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.” Verse 2 is how he accomplishes that.

“But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.” Day and night. This begins a chain showing the consistency with which we should seek this nourishment, this daily bread. As the dying man dies, he is giving life to the inner man.

Because he is nourished in his spirit and his delight is in the law of the Lord, he does not even want to sit among the ungodly. When murmurers come to you, consider why they are so comfortable bringing it to you. Bishop brought out the saying, and it is how he deals with people who come to him with that stuff: don't tell me what they say about me; tell me why they feel comfortable telling you. You have to question that and examine it: why is somebody so comfortable coming to you with something you know in your spirit is not right to be spoken? Saying you just heard it and said nothing makes you not the man of Psalm 1. If your delight is in the law of God, the minute you hear evil you will be instant in season to correct it. There is a right way to hear things and handle them, and that is a meditation for you.

precepts.why:
“This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth”: you always keep it with you; you are never without it. “But thou shalt meditate therein day and night.” Day and night again. Prophets separated by hundreds and thousands of years were of one mind and one accord, because they understood the message given to our forefathers in the wilderness: the daily bread, that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.

“That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous.” This is not prosperity doctrine, sow your seed and get money. It is the prosperity in the scriptures, the promises. We are poor now but rich, and we cannot receive that inheritance until all things are fulfilled.

“And then thou shalt have good success.” Then you will be like the man in Psalm 1: not in the counsel of the ungodly, not sitting among sinners, but in the right spirit. It all ties together.

sense.text:
Repetition creates retention, and the Bible is very repetitive for our people. Just as you need vitamin D and certain minerals every day, you need certain aspects of these verses every day, and the Bible as a whole every day.

“O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.” All the day. This is what it means to walk in the spirit and not fulfil the flesh: your mind is stayed on it. When you crave tacos and can't get them until you get off work, you think about them all day and won't eat anything else to spoil your appetite. Where is that same zeal for the word of God?

precepts.why:
“Mine eyes prevent the night watches, that I might meditate in thy word.” In other words: I stay up all night just to consume your word. The watches are the hours of the night when you are supposed to be asleep. As a king with all his responsibilities in the day, David could not wait to get into his private chambers and into the word, and sometimes he did not even sleep.

Some of us were like that in the beginning, meditating all the time. Then, because we stopped nourishing ourselves every day, we lost that yearning. And the Bible is not the same food every day: prophecy, laws, examples, history, exhortation, adventure and action. It is a buffet, a smorgasbord, a cornucopia.

Some days the word gets hold of you, you start sharing it with the brothers, they bring another precept, and an hour goes by. We all have the opportunity to build ourselves today.

sense.text:
“Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart.” Your heart is your mind. Do that, and you can say you have the mind of Christ, the mind of God.

And he gives wisdom at your own desire: if you want it, he will feed you; if you are hungry, he will give it. But you have to be on it. That is why it says to seek out the book of the Lord and read. All of this our forefathers understood, and we have lacked it. Because of religions and denominations, many still have practices not conducive to being an Israelite and taking hold of our heritage and customs. Use this world, but don't abuse it. Balance does not mean half in the world and half here; it means this, the way all our forefathers moved.

precepts.why:
“And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge”: that is the retention, not being on it day and night. Since you do not want your daily bread, God says, all right, now I won't give it. “God gave them over to a reprobate mind.” That is what you want, so that is what you get, and now everything is contrary to God and to the commandments.

That is how someone drifts back, a dog to his vomit. A dog vomits, and as soon as it recovers it starts eating it again. There is hardly a more fitting similitude for being in this truth, killing the old man and leaving those things behind, and then going back to them. They become alluring for reasons you can't understand, the very things you were ashamed of once upon a time when you repented.

sense.text:
“But he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High”: you have to give it. That is leaning not on your own understanding; you give your mind to the Lord the same way you thought about those tacos all day. “And is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.” You are always in the scripture. The first fourteen or fifteen verses of this chapter are a step-by-step instruction on how to increase in wisdom and understanding.

So it was always designed to be daily bread, a dependency. In psychology dependency is a bad thing, but not when it comes to the Lord. Then comes the problem of the flesh: people laugh and nod, and walk out with the same habits.

Bishop Nathanyel gave us a template with the four chapters, and with study, pray, apply. But I can put the steak in front of you, and if you don't chew it and digest it, it means nothing. People follow Instagram fads religiously, lemon water every day, eat this not that, but won't do religious things religiously, and our religion is the laws, the Bible.

The Bible does not present men as spiritually neutral: you are cold or hot, and the lukewarm are spewed out. The flesh is always pulling and the spirit is always fighting.

“For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other.” We read it, we know it, and we do nothing about it, or not enough. “So that ye cannot do the things that ye would”: there is always a pull against what you want to do. The spirit pulls you from the fleshly things and the fleshly things pull you from the spiritual. That is what Paul is talking about in Romans 7, where he sounds like he is bugging out if you don't know what you are reading.

precepts.why:
These are other words for Galatians 5:17: “Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” We must embrace that. You know when you are hungry; some are so used to food in their mouth it is not even hunger. Carry that over to the scriptures, and you will go from level one to level five.

Coming out of Egypt, we were receiving the laws in that regeneration and being reminded what to stay away from and what to cleave to. There is the didactic part of learning, the theoretical instruction through lectures and readings, and then the application, the hands-on execution that tests the knowledge through practical experience: testing, proving. An electrician or plumber reads all the books, but on the job he is an apprentice, then a journeyman, and so on. The wilderness was the opportunity not just to hear the word but to apply it and consume it. Every repetition reinforces something in you, and that is how he establishes your mind, so that when the problem comes your response is instant, in season and out of season. Reading alone is not the point, but without it in your mind you will fall short when the time for application comes.

sense.text: “For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.” Where your treasure is, there will your heart be. If you are after the flesh, you will mind the things of the flesh.

“For to be carnally minded is death.” If you stay in that carnal mind, that is death. “But to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” Notice: not just life, but peace. Some still have so much drama in their lives because they are not applying this; they have no peace because they are seeking peace in things that are not God. The peace of God passes all things and overcomes whatever you are dealing with. Those who say it doesn't work for them are still not applying what they need to apply.

precepts.why: Read with “to be carnally minded is death”: “What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.” The fruit of the things you now realize were sinful behavior, the things you should be ashamed of, is death. He is dealing with carnality.

On that peace, and on how we are pulled away from God when we are not feeding ourselves: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.” It is heavy, because it says trust in him. Saying it doesn't work for you shows that you don't trust God. It is unbelievable how much goes back to your faith. If you are weak in spirit, your faith is weak too. If you can't see the value in what we are doing and trying to put forth, or can't find and trust in God, you are weak in faith. If your faith is only strong when things are going your way, that is not faith at all. If it is only when things benefit you that you feel confident trusting God, then you don't trust in God.

The mind stayed on him is the meditation: when we meditate day and night on the Lord, we build up our trust in him. That is what the second generation in the wilderness had to do, and the first generation did not.

sense.text:
How crazy the body is, how crazy the flesh is: “the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.” Madness is in our heart. If it is not of God, it is craziness. If you feel crazy, it is normal; just don't act on it. This place will drive you mad. Pressure makes you mad, not just crazy but angry and frustrated.

Knowing that is the condition of our flesh, we have to acknowledge that we have a tendency to drift. It is natural; it is what the body and carnal-mindedness do. It does not always show itself as rebellion. Rebellion is the escalation, the next level of drifting: when you give in to the drift, it becomes the willful, I know that's wrong, but I'm going to do it.

“They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel.” This is what happened in the wilderness, and it did not take long: soon. Our minds can't fathom what those miracles looked like; we did not witness them with our own eyes, and they are only as strong as our imagination. But they were all witnesses under that cloud. Despite the deliverance from Egypt, they saw God's power first hand in the wilderness, and they forgot.

That is when God devised the manna: maybe with this they will see a spiritual message, that they need me, that I took them out of that hard bondage. They were willing to go back into captivity to have their bellies filled.

“But lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert.” We hear lust and think sex right away. But what were they lusting for? The meat pots, the leeks and the onions, everything Egypt provided for them, despite the miracles.

This is how we drift. “Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.” Let them slip is to let them run out as leaking vessels: there is always leakage if you don't refill it. You have to take more earnest heed.

Hebrews is written to Jews, scribes and Pharisees who knew the Old Testament; it speaks of things without explaining them. If you don't understand the Old Testament, you won't get Hebrews.

Boats don't have to fight the current; they just stop rowing, and the current takes them. Stop kicking against the pricks, go with the program, and you will wind up all right.
“I will delight myself in thy statutes: I will not forget thy word.” This is the whole theme: we drift, and we need to be nourished daily.

precepts.why: “I will never forget thy precepts: for with them thou hast quickened me.” The precepts are not forgotten because by them he was quickened. They are spirit and they are life.

David is writing about this because he experiences that drift. We look past it, but he is telling you, I deal with these things too, and I do these other things so that I won't forget. “My soul is continually in my hand: yet do I not forget thy law.” That is retention.

“I have gone astray like a lost sheep.” Here is the acknowledgement. Everything he said in this psalm, about the laws, the truth, not forgetting, meditating, leads up to this last verse, where he acknowledges why he went the way he did. We know his sin, and he is letting you know how he got to it. That is how any of us goes from one point to the next: the lack of daily nourishment, the lack of meditation.

“Seek thy servant; for I do not forget thy commandments.”

sense.text:
It was not just David. As a people, the whole northern kingdom forgot all that was established. “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge”: the lack of knowledge leads to our destruction. “Because thou hast rejected knowledge”: how do you reject it? By not consuming it daily. “I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.”

When a school or a camp has a dead spirit, you can be sure they are not consuming the word daily. You can look busy, go out to camp, do missions and every program, but if the individuals are not consuming the word the way they need to, they are dead spirits. Of course they are dead: they are not eating; they are not feeding the spirit.

What makes it all more challenging is the veil of flesh. Even with everything we see and know, it is like looking through a veil. Think of a wedding veil: it is see-through, but not clearly. Put the camera behind it, as some movies do, and you can make out the outlines of things but not see them. That is what it is like to be in this flesh, and you have to understand the reality of why we dwell inside the mortal flesh.

“By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh.” Christ's flesh is called a veil. Our bodies are the same: they almost keep us from seeing anything spiritual clearly. So what we can see must be treated as that much more precious, and that is why it is even more important to nourish our spirits daily. That veil is the flesh.
“For the thoughts of mortal men are miserable, and our devices are but uncertain”, because we are in this veil.

“For the corruptible body presseth down the soul”: this is the body, corruptible, the thing that makes us drift. It presses down the soul, and it goes back to Galatians 5:17.

“And the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” You are going to meditate on something. Your mind is never void and blank; you are always meditating on something. That is why you have to direct your paths, and meditate on the scriptures.

“And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth.” Our understanding of the scriptures comes through great labor and through revelation; God has to give it to you, and God gives the increase. And the veil of the flesh makes it difficult. We are often wrong when we are not in the spirit and not looking through the lens of the scriptures, and how can you look through it if you are not studying? You won't even know what verse to go to for your nourishment.

“And with labour do we find the things that are before us”: that labor is consuming the word every day. “But the things that are in heaven who hath searched out?” We are always preoccupied with the fleshly, the carnal.

“And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above?” This is how God gives the wisdom. He sends the Holy Spirit from above just as the manna was sent from above, the spiritual meat.

“For so the ways of them which lived on the earth were reformed”: that is how the souls of those who live on the earth are reformed. “And men were taught the things that are pleasing unto thee”: we know what is right for God and what is wrong. “And were saved through wisdom.”

This explains why understanding needs continual renewal. When you start drifting, verses like this are what should come to your head to anchor you. It starts with acknowledgement: think of the verses on the flesh, on drifting, on consuming the word every day, and it gives you a hard stop. Then you can assess and get precise about which scriptures you need to meditate on for what you are dealing with. Until you acknowledge that you are going off, you can't prescribe what you need. That is what leads people to drift to the point that they walk away: they did not want to retain all this in their knowledge.

precepts.why: “My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.” The flesh and the heart are going to fail, but God is the strength of the heart and our portion for ever.

sense.text:
“But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind.” That is Galatians 5:17. The mind is where the soul resides, and the flesh is fighting the soul, the spirit. “And bringing me into captivity to the law of sin”: that is its purpose, to bring you into the things whose end is death. “Which is in my members”: it is in the body.

Anybody who pretends it is not present in them will not endure in this walk. You have to acknowledge your vices and your members, because you have members for good and members for evil, for sin. Own those things.

“O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?” This body is a body of death. From the day you are born you are heading towards death, and the only thing on the other side of that is the preservation of your soul, which only God can do. That is why you fear God, who can destroy body and soul, and not men, who can only destroy the body.

“For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved”: the flesh is a veil, and here it is also an earthly house called a tabernacle. A tabernacle is a place where you dwell. This body is only a place for the soul to reside in this realm, this present world. “We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.”

“For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven.” In this body we groan. We have a real house, a real tabernacle for our spirit, where we don't have to fight: not full of gas, no incontinence, the back doesn't hurt, the feet don't stink. Everything that comes with this body draws us and is always fighting our spirit. As your spirit grows in understanding, it is like living with a spouse you hate and who hates you; before you understood, you were quite comfortable in that relationship with your body. That is why it says to mortify your members: you have to cut it off.
“If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.” Right now we are without defense, which is why we are told to put on the whole armor of God.

“For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened.” This body is a pain; it presses us down, as in Wisdom of Solomon 9. “Not for that we would be unclothed”: not that we want to be without a tabernacle; it is just this one we don't want. “But clothed upon”, with the one that is waiting for us, fit for us, “that mortality might be swallowed up of life”, with eternal life.

precepts.why:
To sum up what Paul said: “even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” We are spiritual souls groaning within our carnal selves. That adoption is the redemption of our real body. No body we have had here is your real body; that is not how you look, and it is not the perfection waiting for us after Christ returns.

That is why bodily exercise profits little. It will not lead you to salvation, but there is profit in it to maintain your vessel. You have to respect it, because it is the only one you have: if you knew you would never get another car, you would do all the maintenance. So you don't neglect the body, but we yearn to get out of the groaning.

There are many threads you could follow from here, and everybody gets excited about the spiritual body. You don't need that. You need some bread, some daily bread.

sense.text:
Back to the veil. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.” Christ's body was a veil, our flesh is a veil, this body is a tabernacle we groan in while we wait for the redemption of our bodies. We see through this veil. Then we will see face to face, when we have our real body and are no longer obstructed by the groanings of this physical body.

The only way to have clarity in this body is to feed your spirit every day in some way: audio classes, a few verses, even when the day was too intense for your four chapters. Four chapters is the standard, but whatever happens, engage with God's word every day. We don't perceive everything perfectly: the flesh obscures, distracts, and presses down the soul.

The glass is like a mirror, and it is hard to see your true inner man, the spiritual man, in this flesh. The only way to get some clarity is to wipe that mirror clean, and you do that by feeding yourself daily. Christ is in you unless you are reprobate, and the first steps to becoming reprobate are not consuming the word every day.

A lot of people don't really want to engage with the scriptures because they show you things about yourself that are uncomfortable for your flesh to see. Your spirit rejoices to find those things, because it knows it can change something, but many are averse because they are more preoccupied with feeding the flesh.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” You are just a hearer if you come on Saturday and do nothing to feed your spirit the rest of the week, or do it every other day, or every four days. It is daily.
“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass”: his carnal self. He feeds and nourishes the carnal self.

“For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way”: I am carnal, a physical man. “And straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was”: he forgot the inner man, the spiritual man, and he is out there naked, without the armor of God.

“But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty”: he feeds himself, meditates day and night, has that desire, that hunger and thirst for righteousness. “And continueth therein”: that is the part we glaze over. That is the daily. Class was fire, that was great, and then nothing; you don't continue therein.

“He being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his doings, just as Joshua 1:8 says to meditate and not let it depart, and then thy way will prosper. All the forefathers, separated by years and spaces of time, spoke with one accord. Go the opposite way of this, and you become a forgetful hearer.

Think of fasting in reverse. We fast to deny the body food and drink and show we have power to deny ourselves other things. But the hunger and thirst you feel when you fast is what happens to your soul when you don't give it the word every day: the headache, the hunger, the weakness. It is hungry, tired, can't think right, blurry and hazy. That is how your inner man feels when you deny it God's word.

You have to come to the point where you truly believe that if you don't consume this book and pray, you are going to die, and you will. Pray three times a day as we are supposed to; missing the noon prayer when caught up shows how you drift. It is not enough to just show up, and not enough to wear your fringes. It is never enough.

“But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.” You have to find that somewhere deep down inside you.

precepts.why: “Blessed is the man that doth meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding.” That reasoning is what is really happening in Romans 7 and Galatians 5 and in what the forefathers spoke of. There is a reasoning that goes on in your head. The old picture of Satan on one shoulder and an angel on the other is real, and it happens in every interaction you have.

sense.text:
“Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away”, but only if you retain it. Wisdom lets you know to do what you need to do to retain it.

“Yea, she is easily seen of them that love her”: it becomes clear. The veil is not so obscure, not so dark, but only if you love her. “And found of such as seek her”: only of those who seek her. Your desire has to be that you want it, that you need it.

“And be not conformed to this world”: to be conformed to this world is to be focused only on the things of this world and not feed the spiritual. People ask how not to be conformed; this is how.

“But be ye transformed”: that is the transformation science calls neuroplasticity, the brain's lifelong capacity to rewire itself in response to learning. These are observations science makes of what God already put in place in our bodies. The connections in the brain strengthen or weaken depending on how often they are used. Feed the flesh, and the flesh stays strong; feed the spirit, and the spirit gets strong and overcomes the flesh. When you start repenting, your brain starts changing in structure and function, and you maintain that by nourishing it daily. Significant rewiring, really putting the old man to bed, needs constant, daily, repetitive and often difficult stimulation, which can become exhausting and difficult to maintain.

That is the fight of the flesh against the spirit that we glaze over: a literal process in your brain every day. That is why the scripture speaks of the feeble knees and the faint hands, and says not to be weary in well doing. There will be days you are tired, and it is hard to pick up this book and fill yourself with it. That is when you have to press even more.

“By the renewing of your mind”: every day you give it the scriptures, every day your mind is in something biblical. Then when the punch comes and you are not ready, you react instantly and know how to deal with the situation, like the martial arts student who blocked a punch out of nowhere after months of boring repetition.

“That ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” This ties back to Exodus, Deuteronomy and Matthew: they were taught the things pleasing to God; we know what he wants; and we prove it by the transformation of the mind.

If you train consistently for six months your body changes, and if you stop for six months it regresses. You don't expect one workout to last forever, so why expect one class, one feast day, one emotional moment to carry you indefinitely? Daily lust strengthens lust: every time you hit that porn, it strengthens lust. Daily anger strengthens anger, and daily worldliness strengthens worldliness. But daily meditation strengthens godliness, daily study strengthens understanding, and daily prayer, communing with the Lord, strengthens spiritual awareness.

precepts.why: “But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” By reason of use: repeated practice, repeated exposure, repeated exercise. That is how the renewing of the mind works.

sense.text: The renewal of the inner man: how do we renew him? “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.” Daily, again. You deny yourself by feeding the spiritual man: deny the carnal, feed the spiritual.

precepts.why: “I die daily.” This goes with the daily. How do you do it? By feeding: you starve the carnal man, not by refusing food, but in the things of the spirit, and you feed the spiritual man.

“But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”: that is the dying daily. “Lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” He preaches to others, but he knows he will drift if he does not die daily and give life to the spiritual man daily.

“For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.” You can't do that without constant connection to the scriptures. Many have issues, depression, sin, and say they are battling. You ain't battling nothing; you don't even open your Bible every day. You say you are enduring; enduring what? The spirit trying to tell you to do right?

Why do people who seemed to have good works and a good reputation move to the left or to the right? They stopped feeding themselves daily. That is scary, and it is a reason to check yourself. There is no excuse anymore: you have a Bible with you all the time, Bible apps, a verse of the day, even streaks that reward you for every day. It does not always have to be formal. Get so familiar with your scriptures that you know where a verse sits on the page.

sense.text: Now the dying man. “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth”: mortify the carnal members, “fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry”, just to name a few. You have to kill it, and then you have to renew.

“For which cause we faint not”: it gets exhausting and tiring, yet we faint not. “But though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.” Day by day. As with the rewiring of the mind day by day, there is a physical change happening in you as you feed your spirit. The outward man dies; the inward man must be fed. Daily bread for a dying man.

precepts.why:
“That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man.” It is all about strengthening the inner man.

Bodily exercise profits little. That does not mean don't do it, but it is not everything. In that time the Greeks and Romans were all about appearance and vanity and idolized the perfect body. It profits a little, but what you have to strengthen day by day is the inner man, “That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.”

“Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom”: let it dwell in you, strengthening the inner man, “teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.”

sense.text: “Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.” That is how you keep your defenses up: the word has to stay in your heart. It goes back to Galatians 5, walk in the spirit and you won't fulfil the flesh, and to Romans 7, the duality in man.

precepts.why: “This is my comfort in my affliction: for thy word hath quickened me.” The word quickens. Remember that quickening for the close.

sense.text: “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” His compassions are the grace we have to renew ourselves every day.

“They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” Notice the pattern through all of this: daily bread, daily mercy, take up your cross daily, daily death, daily renewal. The Bible says every day, and in some verses many times a day, but we are doing a once-a-week thing.

Examine yourself. Many of us do things in the body, for the school and the offices, and all of that is good, but are you doing your daily work, feeding yourself daily? Without that daily, you are not going to make it. If you have found yourself questioning your walk or weary in it, it is almost certainly because you are not in this word daily as you need to be.

What happens when you stop eating? These are the steps that lead to being reprobate, not wanting to retain God in your mind. “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord God, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord.”

He did this to us as a people in different captivities, and it can happen to you as an individual, as in Romans 1:28. They soon forgot his works. If they saw miracles and still went off, what makes you think you will last without daily sustenance in this word? It is not going to work.

Back to the manna. “Instead whereof thou feddest thine own people with angels’ food”: that is the manna, “and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.” One man loves cheesecake and another doesn't, but the manna tasted however it needed to taste for you: sweeter for the one who likes it sweet, subtly sweet for the one who likes it subtle. Every man to his taste, and that is spiritual.

“For thy sustenance declared thy sweetness unto thy children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.” So don't just read. Some are averse to reading the verses that deal with what they are dealing with. Feed yourself with what you need, and you can't do that if you are not in there looking every day. Some study everything except what is eating at them, because they don't want to fix it. The manna pleased everyone, some took more and some less, and it filled them and nourished them with what they needed.

precepts.why: Why did he do this? “That thy children, O Lord, whom thou lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourisheth man”: it is not physical food, “but that it is thy word, which preserveth them that put their trust in thee.” That is how we are preserved, and the manna represents that. It goes back to Deuteronomy 8: it was never about feeding their stomachs. It was teaching what truly preserves life, lining us up to accept and receive Christ.

sense.text: Now we know the flesh presses us down, that we drift, that we forget, and that we need daily renewal and daily bread. “Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.” Christ is about to open you up.
“Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.” Moses did not give it to you; the Father gives the true bread from heaven.
“For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.” He is talking about himself.

“Lord, evermore give us this bread.” “I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.” What happened with the manna was always symbolic of Christ. When it says it was a shadow, a foreshadowing, that is everything: from beginning to end, Christ is in it, and it was all for us to know and see and understand.

So boo-hoo on Christians who say the New Testament is greater than the Old, because the Old established everything else. That is why you need here a little, there a little; that is how you unlock the scriptures.

precepts.why: This goes into the bread of life: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” He is the way, the truth and the life, and by him we know the Father.
He is the way, and we have to walk as he walked: “He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.”

He is also the truth. He fulfilled, and will fulfil, all prophecies: Lo, I come in the volume of the book. “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” This is speaking of Christ, the embodiment of all these things.

Then he is the life: “But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst.” He is that sustenance again. In 1 Corinthians 10 they all ate the same spiritual meat and all drank the same spiritual drink. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.”

“He that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.” Christians will say that record is exclusively the New Testament. The record God gave of his Son is the whole Bible, starting in the Old Testament. When these letters were written, they had at best the gospels and the testimonies. Where was that record found? In the Old Testament: the manna, the cloud, the rock, the water that came out of it so that they could live. It physically happened so that we could have it today.

“And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son”: that is the daily bread, the daily nourishment. “He that hath the Son hath life”: that is the bread, the sustenance from heaven, the Holy Spirit. “And he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.” It is not just saying I accept Christ; it is everything read up to this point, and the whole Bible in its totality.
“I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.” You want to get to the Most High? You have to enter in through him. “And shall go in and out, and find pasture”, and find that rest.
He is the life: “For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.”

sense.text: “I am that bread of life.” How many times does he have to say it?
“Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead.” He is talking about what the manna represented. Christ is that manna.
“This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.”

“I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.” His flesh was his veil, and he would sacrifice that form. His blood would be spilled, above the law of sacrifice, so that we can have this grace period to repent.

precepts.why:
“As the living Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father: so he that eateth me, even he shall live by me.” What does it mean to eat of him? Consume his word every day.

The Pharisees were offended when he said such things, and shame on them, because they knew the Old Testament. That is why Paul went in on them in Hebrews 5, that they needed milk again: they had forgotten that all of it foretold Christ. How were his words hard for those who had studied the foundation? We feed upon Christ through his words.

sense.text: This should give you a new perspective: “And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.”

precepts.why: “The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.” We are all partakers of that manna.

We do this every Sabbath, and here is another reason to take it seriously: “the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.”

The broken bread, the remembrance, the body, the sacrifice: he is the true manna. You break bread every time we come together, but you are not eating the bread that is abundant for us. Break your bread once a week and think that is all right? The breaking of bread is also symbolic of the manna, and of the commitment we have to consume God's word every day, day and night.

sense.text:
“To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.” That is eternal life, and seeing clearly at that point. He will give him to eat of the hidden manna.

So remember: the body is dying; you are born on a path to death. The flesh fights, the mind forgets, and we are prone to forget. The soul is weighed down by this veil, this tabernacle. So the inward man has to be renewed, kept alive by the word every day. The manna showed it, the prophets lived it and spoke of it, David meditated on it heavily, Paul explained it thoroughly, and Christ revealed himself at the end to be that manna, the true bread from heaven.

“It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” That is the spirit and the life Christ meant: the true bread from heaven, his words. That should give us a more profound understanding.

In the wilderness we had to sacrifice daily, twice daily. Coming in once a week and feeding yourself so sparingly, you would not understand this. “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.”

“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” If we really considered our ways, the things we think and our behavior, we would understand why we need to seek him daily, continually, to forgive us of our sins.
